4.text: oppression; demand of tribute (hitherto wholly unknown); exactions from the

5.text: officials and Cossacks, who succeeded in enslaving a number of the strongest

6.text: men and women; and the fraudulent acts of the merchants, who imposed on

7.text: all those that remained free the burden of interminable debts. Then came

8.text: contagious diseases, which made havoc not only among the natives, but also

9.text: among the conquerors, who lived under the same material conditions.

10.text: Worst of all, the natives lost their vital energy and their zest for life,

11.text: which gave them the power and the will to struggle with the harsh Arctic

12.text: nature. A number of them abstained from matrimony and from producing

13.text: offspring. They dropped a large part of their former pursuits, and patiently

14.text: submitted to regular periods of famine, considering their tribe doomed to

15.text: destruction. For instance, among the vanishing clans of the Yukaghir on the

16.text: Lower Kolyma the number of unmarried people is disproportionately large.

17.text: The hunting of reindeer and the capturing of moulting birds to a considerable

18.text: degree went out of practice, because they required too much exertion. The

19.text: people live solely by fishing, and every spring suffer from the scarcity of food,

20.text: often amounting to a real famine. It must not be forgotten that also under

21.text: the natural condition of affairs before the arrival of the Russians, the increase

22.text: of population, even among the strongest tribes, was very uncertain, and was

23.text: continually checked by war and famine.
